sw.text: Mapumziko ya chakula ni saa saba mchana.
sw.note: One in the afternoon is saa saba mchana.

en.text: Congratulations, you got the job.
Why did you leave that job?
Do you have any questions?
Is there an M-Pesa agent near here?

sw.text: Kuna wakala wa M-Pesa karibu na hapa?
sw.note: Wakala = agent: the small shop that pays out M-Pesa cash.

en.text: How much do you want to withdraw?
I want to withdraw five thousand.

sw.note: Kutoa pesa = withdraw; kuweka pesa = deposit.

en.text: I don't have enough cash right now.

sw.text: Sina pesa taslimu za kutosha sasa hivi.

en.text: How much can you give me?
I can give you three thousand.
Okay, I'll withdraw three thousand.
Do you have your ID?

sw.note: Kitambulisho = ID card, from ku-tambulisha, to make known.

en.text: Yes, here it is.

sw.note: Hiki fits a ki- word like kitambulisho. A card is hii hapa.

en.text: Write your ID number in the book.

sw.text: Andika namba ya kitambulisho kwenye kitabu.

en.text: Okay. What's the agent number?

sw.text: Sawa. Namba ya wakala ni ngapi?

en.text: It's written on the board there.
Done. Have you got the message?
Got it. Count your money.
It's all there, thank you.

sw.note: Pesa takes zi-: pesa ziko, pesa zimeingia.

en.text: I want to deposit two thousand.
Whose number is this?
It's my brother's number.
I want to send money to my mother.

sw.note: ku-m-tum-ia = to-her-send-to: the person comes before the money.

en.text: What's the charge for sending five thousand?

sw.text: Gharama ya kutuma elfu tano ni ngapi?

en.text: I'll send it to you on M-Pesa.
Has the money come in?
Why was I charged so much?

sw.note: Kukatwa = to have money taken off, for fees and deductions.

en.text: I sent money to the wrong number.

alt: Nimetuma pesa kwa namba isiyo sahihi.

en.text: Sorry to hear that. When did you send it?

sw.note: Pole is sympathy for someone's trouble; samahani is an apology.

en.text: Ten minutes ago.
Call customer care quickly.

sw.text: Piga simu huduma kwa wateja haraka.
sw.note: Huduma kwa wateja = customer care; many people just say customer care.

en.text: Can the money be reversed?
Yes, if they haven't withdrawn it.
Okay, I'll call them right now.
Don't give anyone your PIN.

sw.note: Customer care never asks for your PIN.

en.text: Thanks for the advice.
Someone sent me money by mistake.

sw.note: A common trick: let customer care reverse it, don't send it yourself.

en.text: Someone called me asking for my PIN.

sw.text: Mtu fulani alinipigia simu akiomba PIN yangu.
sw.note: a-ki-omba: -ki- means 'while' (while asking).

en.text: Please block my M-Pesa. My phone was stolen.

sw.text: Tafadhali zuia M-Pesa yangu. Simu yangu imeibiwa.

en.text: I want to pay my water bill.
What's the paybill number?

sw.note: Paybill: a company's M-Pesa number for bills and fees.

en.text: What do I put as the account number?

sw.text: Niweke nini kama namba ya akaunti?

en.text: Put the account number that's on the bill.

sw.text: Weka namba ya akaunti iliyo kwenye bili.

en.text: This account number is wrong.

sw.text: Namba hii ya akaunti si sahihi.

en.text: I paid the bill, but it doesn't show.
I paid twice by mistake.
I've come to pay school fees.

sw.note: Karo = school fees.

en.text: Take a number and wait to be called.
The queue is very long today.
It's the end of the month. People got paid.

sw.text: Ni mwisho wa mwezi, watu wamelipwa.

en.text: I'd like to open an account.
What do I need to bring?
Bring your ID and a passport photo.

sw.text: Leta kitambulisho chako na picha ya pasipoti.
sw.note: Leta is the command form of kuleta (never lete).

en.text: Fill in this form.
Sign here, please.

sw.note: Sahihi means both 'signature' and 'correct'.

en.text: I want to deposit money into my account.

sw.text: Nataka kuweka pesa kwenye akaunti yangu.

en.text: What's the account number?
It's my own account.
This note is torn. Can you change it?
Please count it again.
You don't have enough money in the account.

sw.text: Huna pesa za kutosha kwenye akaunti.

en.text: My salary hasn't come in yet.

sw.note: Mshahara is an m- word: mshahara wangu, haujaingia.

en.text: I'd like a statement for the last three months.

sw.text: Naomba taarifa ya akaunti ya miezi mitatu iliyopita.
alt: Naomba statement ya miezi mitatu iliyopita.

en.text: I want to ask about a loan.
The network is down right now.
Is there an ATM near here?
The machine swallowed my card.
I've forgotten my PIN.
Your new card will be ready next week.

sw.text: Kadi yako mpya itakuwa tayari wiki ijayo.

en.text: How do I check my balance?

sw.note: The -je ending asks how: nitaangalia-je = how will I check?

en.text: Are you hungry?

sw.note: Swahili has hunger: una njaa = you have hunger.

en.text: I want milk.
Drink your milk.

sw.note: kunywa keeps its ku- even as a command.

en.text: Finish your porridge.

sw.note: uji = porridge, often a Kenyan child's first meal of the day.

en.text: Are you full?
Wash your hands before you eat.

sw.note: kunawa = to wash your hands or face.

en.text: Don't touch that, it's hot.

sw.note: u-si-guse = don't touch: a 'don't' command ends in -e.

en.text: Don't put that in your mouth.
Hold my hand.
Don't run on the road.
Come here, my child.

sw.note: Njoo = come, to one child; to several: Njooni.

en.text: I fell down.
Sorry, are you hurt?

sw.note: Pole = sorry for your pain, not an apology.

en.text: It hurts here.
Don't cry, I'm here.
Why are you crying?
He snatched my ball.

sw.note: kunyang'anya = to snatch from someone.

en.text: Say sorry to your sister.

sw.note: mw-ambie = tell him or her.

en.text: Share the biscuits with your brother.

sw.note: gawana = share out with each other.

en.text: Say thank you.
Can I go and play outside?

sw.note: ni-ka-cheze = may I go and play? -ka- means go and.

en.text: Let's go and play outside.
Who wants a bath?
Close your eyes, or the soap will sting.

sw.note: kuwasha = to sting or itch.

en.text: Have you brushed your teeth?

sw.note: kupiga mswaki = to brush your teeth (mswaki = toothbrush).

en.text: Brush your teeth before bed.
I don't want to sleep.
It's time for bed.
Read me a story.

sw.note: ni-some-e = read for me.

en.text: Shall I tell you a story?

sw.note: ni-ku-simulie = shall I tell you?

en.text: One more story, then you sleep.
I'm scared.
Sleep well, my child.
I love you so much.
Don't make noise, the baby is sleeping.

sw.note: amelala = is asleep (has lain down).

en.text: It will only hurt a little.
You're very brave.
We've come for the baby's vaccine.

alt: Tumekuja kwa ajili ya chanjo ya mtoto.
sw.note: a-pate = so that he or she gets.

en.text: Do you have the clinic card?

sw.note: The clinic card records every weight and vaccine.

en.text: Sorry, I forgot the clinic card at home.

sw.text: Samahani, nimesahau kadi ya kliniki nyumbani.
alt: Samahani, nimesahau kitabu cha kliniki nyumbani.

en.text: Next time, don't forget the clinic card.

sw.text: Siku nyingine usisahau kadi ya kliniki.
sw.note: u-si-sahau = don't forget.

en.text: Okay, I'll bring it next time.

sw.note: ni-ta-i-leta: i- stands for kadi (the card).

en.text: How many months old is the baby?
She's nine months old.
Bring her here so we can weigh her.

sw.note: tu-m-pime = so we can measure her.

en.text: Here she is.
She's gained weight well.
Does she have any problems?
She's had diarrhoea since yesterday.
Give her plenty of water.
Okay, I'll do that.
She doesn't want to eat.
He cries a lot at night.
He's teething.

sw.note: kuota meno = to cut teeth (ota = grow, sprout).

en.text: Today is her measles vaccine.

sw.text: Leo ni chanjo yake ya surua.

en.text: Will it hurt much?
Only a little. Hold her firmly on your lap.

sw.note: mapajani = on the lap (mapaja = thighs).

en.text: She may get a slight fever.
What should I do if she gets a fever?

sw.note: a-ki-pata = if she gets.

en.text: Give her this medicine three times a day.

sw.text: Mpe dawa hii mara tatu kwa siku.

en.text: When is the next vaccine?

sw.note: i-na-yo-fuata = which follows (chanjo takes i- words).

en.text: Come back in one month.
When should I start giving her porridge?
Start giving her porridge at six months.

sw.text: Anza kumpa uji akifikisha miezi sita.

en.text: Don't give him sweets.

sw.note: peremende and pipi both mean sweets.

en.text: Put him to bed at eight.

sw.note: saa mbili usiku = eight at night: hours count from dawn.

en.text: Please change her nappy.

sw.note: nepi = nappy or diaper.

en.text: How old is your baby?
She's one year old.
He's started walking.
Where are you travelling to?
One ticket to Nairobi, please.

alt: Nipe tiketi moja ya Nairobi, tafadhali.

en.text: I want to book a seat for tomorrow.

sw.note: kukata tiketi = to buy a ticket (word for word: to cut one).

en.text: For which day?
Is there a night bus tonight?
What time does the bus leave?

sw.note: basi takes li-: basi linaondoka, basi limechelewa.

en.text: Yes, it leaves at eight at night.

sw.note: saa mbili usiku = eight at night: hours count from dawn.

en.text: Where do I board the Nairobi bus?
How much is the ticket?
It's one thousand five hundred.

sw.text: Ni elfu moja na mia tano.

en.text: Is there a cheaper ticket?

sw.text: Kuna tiketi ya bei nafuu zaidi?

en.text: Is there a window seat?
Only the back seats are left.
Okay, I'll take a back seat.
Your name and ID number, please.

sw.text: Jina lako na namba ya kitambulisho, tafadhali.

en.text: Here's my ID.

sw.note: hiki hapa = here it is, for a ki- word like kitambulisho.

en.text: Will you pay cash or by M-Pesa?

sw.text: Utalipa pesa taslimu au kwa M-Pesa?
sw.note: pesa taslimu = cash.

en.text: I'll pay by M-Pesa.
Do you have luggage?
Yes, one big bag.
Be here thirty minutes before departure.

sw.text: Uwe hapa dakika thelathini kabla ya safari.

en.text: So I should come at half past seven?

sw.text: Kwa hiyo nije saa moja na nusu?
sw.note: saa moja na nusu = half past seven: hours count from dawn.

en.text: Yes, and don't be late.

sw.note: u-si-chelewe = you-don't-be late: a don't-request ends in -e.

en.text: I won't be late.
Here's your ticket.
Thank you. What time do we reach Nairobi?
Tomorrow at five in the morning.

sw.text: Kesho saa kumi na moja alfajiri.
sw.note: saa kumi na moja alfajiri = five in the morning.

en.text: Can I change the date on my ticket?

sw.text: Naweza kubadilisha tarehe ya tiketi yangu?

en.text: I missed my bus.

sw.note: Nimeachwa na basi = the bus has left me: I missed it.

en.text: Is there another bus today?
Why is the bus late?
The bus is late. It will leave at eleven in the morning.

sw.text: Basi limechelewa. Litaondoka saa tano asubuhi.

en.text: The bus has broken down near Voi.
My flight is delayed.

sw.note: ndege = plane, and also bird.

en.text: Your flight is forty minutes late.

sw.text: Ndege yako imechelewa kwa dakika arobaini.

en.text: What time should I be at the station?
The train doesn't wait for anyone.

sw.note: The SGR train leaves on the minute.

en.text: Ticket and ID, please.
I forgot my ID at home.
Can I use my passport?
Is my bag too heavy?

sw.note: limezidi uzito = has gone over the weight.

en.text: Your bag is too heavy.
You'll pay for the extra weight.
Can I take this bag on the plane?

sw.text: Naweza kubeba begi hili ndani ya ndege?

en.text: Is this the queue for Mombasa?
My bag hasn't come out yet.
Excuse me, you're in my seat.

sw.note: umekaa = you have sat down: you are sitting.

en.text: Is this seat number twelve?

sw.text: Hiki ni kiti namba kumi na mbili?

en.text: Can we swap seats?

sw.note: kubadilish-ana = to change with each other.

en.text: I'm travelling with my child.
Does a child pay full fare?
Where can I charge my phone?
Does the bus stop on the way?
Where will we stop to eat?
We'll stop here for twenty minutes.
How long do we stop here?
Wait for me, I'm going to the toilet.
Please wake me when we reach Voi.
Are you going all the way to Mombasa?
I'm going home for the holidays.
I've arrived safely.
I'll call you when I arrive.

sw.note: ni-ki-fika = I-when-arrive.

en.text: Taxi? Where are you going?
No, thanks. Someone is coming to pick me up.

sw.text: Hapana, asante. Kuna mtu anakuja kunichukua.

en.text: How much is a taxi to Nyali?
To Nyali, it's two thousand.
Can you help me carry my bags?
(Called at the door: may I come in?)
Welcome! Come in, come in.
My respects, elder.
(Reply to Shikamoo.) Welcome, all of you.
Sit down. How was the journey?
Eat, eat! Don't be shy.
Have some more.
You're leaving already?
Wait, have some tea first.
My child will bring you tea right now.

sw.text: Mtoto wangu atawaletea chai sasa hivi.

en.text: When you get home, greet your mother for me.
I've put aside some oranges for you to take.
Amen. When will you come back again?
Bring your children next time.

sw.text: Mje na watoto wenu mara ijayo.

en.text: Wait, let me walk you to the road.
All right then. Go in peace.
(Marahaba: the elder accepts your respects.) Good morning! How did you sleep?

blurb.en: The first talk of the day at the gate, with an older neighbour: respect greeting first, then the long morning greetings nobody skips.
An open-air vegetable stall run by a mama mboga: prices per kilo or per pile, bargaining is normal, M-Pesa is taken.
A motorbike taxi (bodaboda) from the stage: agree the fare first, guide the rider with left, right and landmarks, pay cash or M-Pesa.
Tea at a small hoteli or in a home: chai is boiled with milk and sugar; on the coast, street sellers pour tiny cups of kahawa in the evening.
The neighbourhood chemist (kemisti or duka la dawa): the pharmacist advises on the spot and tells you the dose in words.
A weekend visit to a family home: call Hodi at the door, greet every elder first, eat what is offered, leave with blessings.
A quick call to make a plan: who you are, when, where, and a bad network.
The office morning: greet everyone one by one, the ten o'clock chai round, a meeting at saa nne, and goodbye in the evening.
